stories.headline: Legal and trust pressure intensified more than model/news hype this cycle
stories.summary: The biggest meaningful change since the March 29 refresh is sharper evidence that rights, provenance, and anti-impersonation concerns are becoming core market structure, not side issues.

stories.headline: BMG added another music-specific copyright front against Anthropic
stories.summary: Reuters reported BMG sued Anthropic over alleged use of copyrighted lyrics in Claude training, citing 493 infringed works and criticizing sourcing from unauthorized torrent sites. That keeps music-specific sourcing and substitution risk very live.

stories.headline: GEMA vs. Suno is now a concrete European test of output similarity and licensing
stories.summary: Music Business Worldwide reported the Munich hearing ended without a ruling and set a June 12 decision date. GEMA is pressing the argument that Suno outputs can be misleadingly similar to original songs in melody, harmony, and rhythm.

stories.headline: Sony says it has already targeted 135,000+ artist deepfakes for removal
stories.summary: Sony's disclosed takedown volume is a strong signal that impersonation is no longer a fringe issue. Trust controls now look like category infrastructure, not just moderation cleanup.

stories.headline: Google distribution and Suno scale still say the category is commercially real
stories.summary: Google is pushing Lyria 3 Pro into mainstream workflow surfaces, and Suno's reported paid scale remains the clearest demand-side proof point in AI music. But those same signals make undifferentiated AI music apps less defensible.

stories.headline: Musician adoption evidence still supports workflow-first products
stories.summary: Moises and Water & Music still show practical tools beating full-song generation in real usage. Stem separation led at 71%, versus 24% for full-song generation, while copyright and authenticity worries stayed high.

stories.headline: X remains more useful as a noise/weather check than a factual source
stories.summary: A small recent-search sample was dominated by hobbyist Suno publishing chatter, Spotify/DistroKid release talk, and scattered user complaints about lyric/copyright flagging. Directionally, that supports the view that AI music is leaking into mass self-publishing workflows and adding downstream trust noise.

themes.workflow_over_hype: The strongest evidence still favors AI tools that remove friction inside existing music workflows rather than tools that fully replace musicians.
themes.rights_cleanliness_matters_more: The legal and commercial environment continues to reward clean sourcing, transparency, and rights clarity.
themes.scale_is_real_but_not_enough: Google's distribution and Suno's scale claim show the category is real, but they also make generic AI music apps less defensible.
themes.trust_infrastructure_is_rising: Sony's deepfake takedowns, Deezer's detection licensing, and Spotify's identity controls all point toward trust/compliance becoming product categories inside music tech.
themes.musio_implication: Musio should keep leaning toward trustworthy creator infrastructure: realistic musical output, human control, workflow fit, and commercially usable results.
